Little Orchard Nursery
Due to the delay in the building of Orchard View Primary Academy we are not able to offer Nursery places to children in September 2026.
We share your disappointment and frustration with this as we understand the importance and positive impact for children attending a Nursery. We also appreciate the importance of nursery provision for parents. We will update this webpage when we have information to share about the planned opening for the 2-year-old plus nursery provision for up to 60 children.
Orchard View Nursery will be a modern and distinctive nursery located within a vibrant, diverse academy community. We believe it will be a truly special place. We will take pride in delivering an ambitious yet adaptable Early Years Curriculum, offering high-quality education provided by qualified, highly skilled teachers, practitioners, and support staff.
We believe it is a privilege to work with young children during such a unique and sensitive stage of their lives. Our nursery will provide a beautifully designed learning environment, tailored to the individual needs of each child, drawing on the deep understanding and expertise from our staff in IFPT’s other nurseries to create the best possible experiences for every child who will be in our care.

Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum
A Bright Start at Orchard View
At Orchard View Primary Academy, our Early Years Foundation Stage is where the Orchard View journey begins. Rooted in our vision of placing pupils at the heart of everything we do, we provide a nurturing, inclusive environment where every child is valued, supported and encouraged to thrive.
Through play, exploration and meaningful experiences, children develop confidence, curiosity and independence as they begin their love of learning. Our EYFS curriculum reflects the values that shape life across our academy. Children learn to work in partnership with others, show respect and kindness, demonstrate integrity by making positive choices, approach challenges with determination, and strive for excellence in all they do.
By creating a safe, happy and stimulating environment, and working closely with families, we ensure every child develops the foundations they need to flourish both academically and socially. In Early Years, we truly live our OVPA motto every day —
"Together we Learn, Together we Succeed."

Arbor Parent Portal
We use Arbor Parent Portal at Inspiring Futures Partnership Trust. All parents/carers are required to use Arbor Parent Portal at Orchard View.
What is the Arbor Parent Portal used for?
Complete required consent forms
Manage payment accounts and make payments directly
Not used Arbor Parent Portal before?
To login into the Parent Portal for the first time and view your child’s dashboard, open the:Arbor SiteClick the “First time logging in” option in the bottom left corner.
Once you have logged in, we recommend that you save the Arbor log in page to your favourites or bookmarks, so you can access it easily in the future. On your first login only, you will need to enter your child’s date of birth to access the dashboard.
Click “Set Password”
Download the app
Whilst you can access Arbor from a browser window on an iPad, iPhone or other mobile device, it works better through the Parent App or via the Parent Portal on a computer.
Enter your email address
More than one child at Orchard View?
If you have more than one child at Orchard View, you can access and view each child through the same portal by clicking on the name at the drop-down menu with the children’s names in the top-left of the home page, then change sibling.
​On doing this for the first time, you will need to enter your other child’s date of birth to access their dashboard.
Have a child at another school using Arbor?
​When you log into the Parent Portal or the Arbor App, you can see details about your children that attend one school using Arbor.If you have two children attending the same school, you can easily switch between students in the app or on the portal.If you have children at more than one school your experience of logging into the Parent Portal and Arbor App will be different. If you use the same email address at both schools, you will be asked which school you want to log into when you log into the app or portal.You won't be able to switch between children on the portal or app if they attend two different schools. This is because each parent at each school will have a separate profile and account with that school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Orchard View Primary - Attendance, Punctuality & Term Time Holidays
pageCache.text:
Attendance, Punctuality & Term Time Holidays
Every child has the right to receive a full time education.
"The law entitles every child of compulsory school age to an efficient, full-time education suitable to their age, aptitude, and any special educational need they may have. It is the legal responsibility of every parent to make sure their child receives that education either by attendance at a school or by education otherwise than at a school.. Where parents decide to have their child registered at school, they have an additional legal duty to ensure their child attends that school regularly. This means their child must attend every day that the school is open, except in a small number of allowable circumstances such as being too ill to attend or being given permission for an absence in advance from the school." Working together to improve school attendance, DfE 2022
Monitoring Attendance & Punctuality
The attendance and punctuality of our pupils is regularly monitored. Registers are taken at 8.50am and at 1:00pm daily. Any absence should be reported to the office by parents before 9am.
We will send a text to parents to request information about their child's absence, if we have not received a notification. This allows us to ensure that pupils are safe and that parents are aware that their child is not in school.
The overall attendance in the academy and the individual attendance of pupils is regularly monitored - all staff hold a responsibility to promote and encourage good attendance at Orchard View.
Our Senior Attendance Champion is:
Our Deputy Attendance Champion is:
Our Attendance Officer is:
call 01296 254042 (leave a message)
Attendance expectations at Orchard View Primary Academy
We want all our pupils to have excellent attendance so they can benefit from the teaching, curriculum, wider experiences and social opportunities that we are providing.
We are acutely aware of the DfE statistics highlighting that pupils who achieve well are noted to have higher levels of attendance, compared to those who do not. We want all OVPA pupils to achieve to the best of their ability.
We are also aware that excellent attendance is a protective factor for pupils who are vulnerable.
We therefore expect parents to support regular attendance at our Academy for their child, except in exceptional circumstances, such as illness, which means that they are unable to safely attend the academy and medical appointments that cannot be scheduled outside of academy time.
The DfE have created this useful guide for parents:
DfE Guide for parents on school attendance
When is a child is too unwell for school?
This can be a difficult decision to make. With some illnesses it is very clear. However, with general coughs, colds and viruses it can be more complicated. A good guide is that if they are struggling to stay awake or are running a high temperature, they should be staying at home. Otherwise, send them to the academy and we will contact you if they are struggling.
There is some guidance here from the NHS which clearly outlines when children should be kept off school for particular conditions: NHS: Is my child too ill for school?
The most common illnesses that you may want information on are listed below:
Attendance for pupils with Medical Conditions or Disabilities
We understand that some pupils will have lower attendance rates due to medical conditions (including mental health) or disabilities requiring regular treatment or medical appointments and that some of these pupils will also have more days when they are too unwell to attend school.
We endeavour to work closely with these families to support regular attendance and get the best outcomes for the child, providing any reasonable adjustments that may be needed. In cases where parents are telling us that low attendance is related to a medical need, we will contact the GP practice for confirmation. We may also ask to contact Bucks School Nursing Team for advice.
What does our academy do regarding attendance?
We monitor attendance daily
We refuse term-time holidays
What can you do to help and support your child with attendance?
Avoid taking any holidays during term time
How do we help and support you?
Punctuality - what if your child is late?
Term time holidays
The DfE are very clear that term-time holidays are not an acceptable reason for a child to be out of school. Their guidance states:
"You have to get permission from the head teacher if you want to take your child out of school during term time.
You can only do this if:
It’s up to the head teacher how many days your child can be away from school if leave is granted."
there are exceptional circumstances
Requesting a planned absence in term time
In line with this guidance, any requests for a planned absence must be submitted prior to the absence using a form which can be collected from the academy office. It is extremely rare that any request for a term time holiday will be authorised by the Head of Academy. While we appreciate that holiday costs rise significantly during school breaks (as this is something that also affects our staff), this will not lead to an authorised request.
Fines for absence in term time
OVPA works with Buckinghamshire Council on term-time absence and refer unauthorised absences of more than 5 days for a fine.
From August 2024, the fine for school absences across the country will be £80 if paid within 21 days, or £160 if paid within 28 days. This rate is in line with inflation and is the first increase since 2012. In the case of repeated fines, if a parent receives a second fine for the same child within any three-year period, this will be charged at the higher rate of £160.
Where there are extenuating circumstances, such as a death or a medical emergency, the Council may stop the fine if they receive relevant evidence. Such evidence must go directly to Buckinghamshire Council, rather than the academy, though we can forward it on to them on your behalf, should you wish.
The fines are applied and received by Buckinghamshire Council and the money does not come to the Academy.
Please read our Attendance Policy for further information:

Medication in the Academy
Prescription Medication:
Where a child needs prescription medication in the Academy, we must have a completed form with all medication details, giving us permission to administer the medication. The most common forms of prescription medication required in the Academy are inhalers, Epi-pens and eczema cream.
We also have an emergency Epi-pen and inhaler stored within the Academy. These are for use by pupils with diagnosed asthma or who already have a prescribed Epi-pen for severe allergies. You will need to provide permission for their use.
To find out more about how we support pupils with specific medical needs at IFPT, please view the 'Supporting Pupils in School with Medical Conditions' policy, here.
It is essential that your child's medical condition records on Arbor are up to date. It is parent/carer responsibility to ensure that these records are correct and that the Academy is informed of all medical conditions.
Antibiotics prescribed three times a day, should be taken at home. For example, in the morning, after-school and in the evening. We only accept antibiotics in the Academy that are prescribed four times a day. Any short-term medication such as this will need to be signed in and out by a parent/carer each day.
What you need to do if your child has required medication:

Academy Travel Plan
Our Academy Travel Plan is supported by the whole academy community and demonstrates our long-term commitment to improving safety and reducing congestion on the roads.
It aims to reduce car use, enable parents and children to choose walking or cycling with confidence and to seek to cut vehicle congestion at the academy gate.
The Academy Travel Plan is a whole academy initiative and demonstrates commitment from children, staff, parents, trustees and the wider community.
Parent Parking
All parents are asked to adhere to a “Parking Promise” and are encouraged to park further away from the academy and walk. If however you find the need to park near or outside the academy, please do not park on bends, on junctions or where the children cross the road. Please also be courteous to our neighbours and do not block driveways.
We are working to build strong relationship with local residents and areas locally. We are confident that we can build strong links with the local community by parking safely and considerately.
Road Safety
Tales of the Road is designed to empower children with the knowledge to stay safe on our road. The resource contains tips and interactive games to help young road users.
Please share the 'Safer Journeys Anthem' below with your child, to support their understanding of road safety:
Modeshift STARS
Modeshift STARS is the national schools awards scheme that has been established to recognise schools that have demonstrated excellence in supporting cycling, walking and other forms of sustainable travel. The scheme encourages schools across the country to join in a major effort to increase levels of sustainable and active travel in order to improve the health and well-being of children and young people.

A PTFA (Parent, Teacher & Friends Association) can:

Build a welcoming school community
Give parents and carers a voice in shaping events and priorities

Please take a look at the IFPT PTFA policy for further information about the PTFA.
If you think you might like to be part of a future PTFA- whether as an organiser, volunteer, or simply someone who supports from time to time- please let us know.
There’s no commitment- just a chance to be kept informed when we’re ready to move forward.
Together, we can build something meaningful for our children and our OVPA community.

Lunches, Milk & Snack
Hot Lunches
At Orchard View Primary Academy, we provide free hot school lunches as part of the Government's Universal Free School Lunches scheme for every pupil in Foundation Stage, Year 1 and Year 2.
Our catering provider is Innovate Impact Food Group (IFG). The food is cooked at The Kingsbrook School and it is delivered fresh each day. Please access the IFG Innovate website HERE to register an account and order lunches for your child.
The link below provides step by step guidance on how to order school meals through the IFG Innovate website:
Ordering school meals guidance
Any queries regarding ordering hot lunches should be directed to IFG Innovate:
Email: primary@impactfood.co.uk
Primary support team 8.30am - 5pm, Monday to Friday
Phone: 0204 542 7211Customer support line 9am - 5pm, Monday - Friday
Eligibility for Pupil Premium and Free School Meals
Families receiving Universal Credit and other benefits may be entitled to receive additional Pupil Premium funding (this is provided directly to the academy) and Free School Meals.
This funding is separate to the free school meals provided under the Government's Universal Free School Lunches scheme for pupils in Foundation Stage, Year 1 and 2 and it also applies to eligible pupils in KS2.
If you think your child may be eligible for Pupil Premium and Free School Meals funding, please complete the application form below and return it to the Academy Office. You can also request a paper copy of this form from the Academy office.
Free School Meals & Pupil Premium Application Form
Milk
You can order milk for your Foundation Stage/KS1 child to have each day by setting up an account with Cool Milk. Milk is free for under 5's and for any pupil eligible for Free School Meals/Pupil Premium funding.
You will be required to pay for your child to receive milk if your child is aged over 5 and they are not eligible for Free School Meals/Pupil Premium funding.
If you no longer wish for your child to receive milk, e.g. if they do not like it, then it is your responsibility to cancel the milk subscription through your account with Cool Milk. This is important in order to avoid unnecessary food wastage.
Healthy Packed Lunches
All pupils who opt out of hot meals, will need to bring in a packed lunch. All packed lunches must be healthy and nutritious,
The following food items are not permitted in packed lunches at Orchard View:
No sweets or chocolate bars X
What to Pack in a Healthy Lunchbox
Guidance from School Health UK on healthy packed lunches can be found here:
School Health UK - Packed Lunch Guidance
Additional ideas for healthy packed lunches can be found here:
BBC Good FoodNHS Change for Life
Carbohydrates
Starchy foods will help your child feel satisfied, as well as being a good source of energy and B vitamins. Choose wholegrain or higher fibre versions with less added fat, salt and sugar. Why not try some of these suggestions?
2 slices of bread
2 small bread rolls
1 tortilla wrap
1 or 2 mini pitta breads
1 scone or currant bun
1 bagel
Fruit and Vegetables
Help your child get their 5 a day by putting two portions of fruit and vegetables in their lunchbox (ideally one fruit and one vegetable).
For younger children (4–6 years), reduce these portion sizes by about half, then increase the amount as they grow. Older primary school children should be eating full portions.
1 cup of grapes, cherries or berries
1 large slice of pineapple or melon
Dairy and Alternatives
Make sure your child is getting enough calcium by putting one of these in their lunchbox or alternatively order milk for your child to receive in school.
Did you know? Low fat milk, cheese and yogurt still has the same amount of calcium as full fat versions, which support growing bones and teeth.
a container/mini-carton of milk (200ml)
2 triangles of spreadable cheese
Beans, Pulses, Fish, Eggs, Meat and Other Proteins
Protein is essential to help your child grow. You should include one of the following in your child’s lunchbox:
Try to include a portion of fish at least once a week. Remember to remove any bones and choose tinned fish in spring water, rather than in brine or oil.
Did you know? Sliced processed meats are higher in salt than meat you have cooked yourself. Why not use leftovers from dinner the night before?
2 slices of cooked meat
2 slices of chicken or turkey breast
1–2 eggs (hard-boiled, sliced or mashed)
Reducing Choking Risks in Young Children
At Orchard View, we follow the Food Standards Agency advice for children aged 5 and under.
Children can choke on food at any age, but the risks are higher in children under 5 years. The guidelines below will help you identify high risk foods that can cause choking and ways to make foods safer for children under 5 years.
We will not allow pupils to eat a food that has not been prepared correctly or is safe for pupils aged 5 and under to eat:
food related choking in young children.pdf
Snacks
All FS/KS1 pupils are provided with a free piece of fruit or veg as a healthy snack each day.
Should you wish to provide your own fruit or veg snack, please place this in your child's book bag in a suitable, sealed container.
KS2 pupils will need to bring in their own snack if required, which must be a piece of fruit or vegetable (no other snacks are permitted in the academy).

Uniform
Academy Uniform
Orchard View Primary Academy is proud of its Academy uniform. We have high expectations and want our pupils to look smart in their uniform each day. We believe that when pupils look smart they gain a sense of pride in themselves and their academy.
We strive to ensure our pupils demonstrate our core values of PRIDE in all that they do:
This includes wearing the correct uniform in the correct way, as well as bringing any necessary equipment that they need.
We ask that polo shirts are tucked in; that jumpers and cardigans are either on or being carried (not tied around waists) and that cardigans are buttoned up, before pupils enter the Academy.
